newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products prices flat to $2 lower.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products prices flat to $2 lower.

text.p: Med oil products were flat to $2 lower on Monday, traders said.
Gas oil slid $2 a tonne across the board, in line with the front month September IPE contract which last traded at $169.25.
Activity was muted. The market remains in the grip of a seasonal summer lull, with many traders on holiday and heating oil requirements minimal.

In the absence of trade assessments of Russian heating oil varied sharply between cif high Med quotes flat to a premium of $1.50/$2. Two cargoes, the Sea Cross and Galea Two, are seen as looking for homes in the absence of a bid.

"The market is not long but relative to buyers it is long," one trader said. Cargoes of En590 are still on the market, and rumoured offered now by a European major and a trading house at around September IPE +$1.

High sulphur cracked fuel cargoes were quiet, assessed unchanged at the $83/$86 mark in the absence of deals but some pressure was said to be looming with Russian material seen coming out after a recent dry spell.
An ISAB stem of 27,000 tonnes was expected to sell around the low cif Med quote, traders said, adding some low sulphur and possibly some high sulphur material was coming out soon from the Black Sea.

With bunker spec avails low in the Med, a refiner was still looking for a cargo in northern Europe, adding it would be prepared to pay high cif Med +$2, while a major was heard bidding $95 cif for bunker spec into Gibraltar.
"Barge prices are not totally attractive and there is little material on offer," the refiner said.
Gasoline values on a very quiet but still relative tight prompt Med market were seen flat or slightly lower on a $1 fall in ARA barges and lower screen levels.
A still firmly closed naphtha arb to the east and a lack of end-user interest within the Med was seen counterbalanced by lack of available volumes.
